identity.title: TANGO: Co-Speech Gesture Video Reenactment with Hierarchical Audio Motion Embedding and Diffusion Interpolation

problem.claim: Generate co-speech body-gesture videos from a short single-speaker reference video and target speech audio, with synchronized gestures.

gap.claim: Existing GVR is limited by audio–motion misalignment and visual artifacts in GAN-generated transition frames.

contributions.claim: TANGO integrates latent-distance gesture retrieval and the hierarchical AuMoClip audio–motion embedding into a graph-based reenactment framework.
ACInterp is a diffusion-based transition-frame generator using a reference motion module and homography background flow for appearance consistency.
The authors report publicly releasing code, pretrained models, and datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish TANGO through hierarchical audio–motion embedding for gesture retrieval and diffusion-based interpolation for transition frames.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TANGO produces realistic, audio-synchronized videos and outperforms existing generative and retrieval methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: TANGO targets co-speech body-gesture video generation from reference video and speech audio.
The framework builds on graph-based GVR and addresses its reported alignment and transition-frame artifact limitations.
Gesture retrieval uses latent feature distance supported by the hierarchical AuMoClip joint embedding space.
ACInterp uses diffusion generation plus motion and background-flow modules to maintain appearance consistency.
The authors report realistic synchronized output and superiority to existing generative and retrieval methods, alongside public release of resources.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps each reported GVR limitation to a named component: AuMoClip addresses audio–motion alignment, while ACInterp addresses transition-frame artifacts and appearance consistency.

lessons.interpretation: Explicit limitation-to-component mapping makes a multimodule contribution easier to evaluate conceptually.
lessons.application: For a system paper, state each motivating failure mode beside the specific design component intended to address it.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when components are exploratory or their targets cannot be separated.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, datasets, baselines, or experimental conditions supporting the reported performance comparison.
It does not specify how many reference videos, speakers, or target utterances are used beyond describing a few-minute single-speaker reference video.
The abstract does not provide ablations isolating AuMoClip, latent-distance retrieval, or ACInterp.
